clips.send: Much of China’s natural gas is in the west — for example under the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang. But most gas is used in the crowded, factory-filled east. The first West–East Gas Pipeline (西气东输 Xī Qì Dōng Shū, “send western gas east”) runs about 4,000 km (2,500 miles) from Lunnan in the Tarim Basin to Shanghai — almost coast to coast across the USA. It went into full operation in 2004.

clips.send: A thermosyphon (热棒 rèbàng, “heat rod”) is a sealed steel pipe: the bottom is buried in the permafrost, the finned top sticks up into the air, and inside is liquid ammonia. In winter the ground is warmer than the air, so the ammonia boils at the bottom, the vapour rises, gives off its heat at the fins, condenses and trickles back down. In summer the air is warmer, so the cycle simply stops.
